title: add kubeadm vendor bundle + local registry-proxy for air-gapped installs
author: Maya Patel
ci_status: pass (linux-integration, smoke-e2e, lint) with one flaky e2e rerun resolved
description: Motivation: Customers running on-prem with kubeadm and strict air-gap constraints requested a self-contained vendor bundle and a small registry-proxy to bootstrap image syncs from operator media. This PR introduces a kubeadm-targeted offline bundle layout, a lightweight registry-proxy that serves the bundled images locally and a set of install-time validators and checksums. The changes aim to reduce manual steps for operators and provide a repeatable install/upgrade flow for kubeadm clusters in disconnected environments. High level changes: 1) bundles/kubeadm/: new bundle layout with images/, manifests/, checksums.txt and a manifest-catalog.json used by the installer to map images to components. 2) installer/airgap/registry-proxy: Dockerfile + minimal Go-based proxy that exposes a small HTTP API to list available images and perform staged pulls into the cluster registry (supports TLS cert injection and basic auth). 3) installer/validators: a kubeadm-specific preflight validator that verifies CRI runtime, kernel settings and bundle integrity via SHA256 checksums. 4) charts/redwood: Helm chart additions to optionally deploy the registry-proxy as a DaemonSet for single-node bootstrap and a ConfigMap-driven imageElectionPolicy for multi-node scenarios. 5) terraform/modules/airgap: a small module to provision a bastion with the proxy in customer VPCs for hybrid installs. 6) docs/airgap-kubeadm.md: step-by-step offline install and upgrade instructions plus rollback guidance and known limitations. The description and checks: implemented checksum verification for every image file, added signature-verification hook (GPG optional), and added conservative defaults for resource requests/limits for the proxy. Testing: unit tests for the proxy image list API, integration smoke tests using kind that simulate disconnected pulls by serving the bundle from a local HTTP server, and full e2e on a small kubeadm VM in our lab. Upgrade path: installer supports in-place upgrades by validating bundle manifests and applying a canary rollout to the registry-proxy and controller deployments; rollback uses Helm rollback of redwood chart and a bundle-rollback script that removes newly loaded images and restores old image tags in the registry. Checklist: [x] bundle layout and sample bundle [x] registry-proxy implementation [x] preflight validators [x] Helm chart toggles and values [x] Terraform module + examples [x] documentation and examples [x] CI smoke tests and e2e run Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative on the proxy feature set (no dynamic mirroring rules yet). Follow-ups are planned to add automated mirror sync tooling and OCI index support. Related: ENG-5128 for product acceptance tests and SUP-789 for customer support case that motivated the work.

release_notes: Add kubeadm-targeted offline bundle and lightweight local registry-proxy to simplify air-gapped installs. Includes preflight validators, Helm toggles, Terraform module for bastion provisioning, and docs for install/upgrade/rollback.
upgrade_notes: To upgrade an existing airgap kubeadm install, prepare a new bundle with manifests/ checksums and upload to the bastion. Run the installer with --bundle-path pointing to the new bundle; installer will validate checksums, apply manifest diffs and perform a canary rollout for the registry-proxy before upgrading controllers. See docs/airgap-kubeadm.md for step-by-step commands.
rollback_instructions: If the upgrade causes regressions, run helm rollback release redwood --namespace redwood to restore previous controller state, then run scripts/bundle-rollback.sh on the bastion to purge newly loaded images and restore registry tags. Consult logs/artifacts in /var/log/redwood-installer for audit trail.
notes: This PR targets kubeadm workflows and intentionally avoids adding RKE2/PKS-specific code. Follow-up PRs will add OCI index support and automated mirror sync agents.
